title: Retain the missing maximal-support operation even when an auxiliary optimum is explicit
statement: For arbitrary rational M, a selector finding Mu=0,u>=0,v=-M^Ty>=0 with u_i v_i=0 and u_i+v_i>0 solves general feasibility: M=[A,-b], last coordinate tau; u_tau>0 yields x=u_first/u_tau, while u_tau=0 implies v_tau=b^Ty>0 and f=-y is a Farkas witness. Standard dual/zero-gap calls then give full LP outputs. S-Conic auxiliary min1^Tz subject Mx-Mz=0,x+w=1,x,z,w>=0 has explicit optimum(0,0,1), but a short walk to it need not discover maximal optimal supports.
